new.title: Walk through the Château de Chenonceau over the Cher
new.desc: The Renaissance château spans the river Cher and is nicknamed the Château des Dames. Henri II gave it in 1547 to Diane de Poitiers, and Catherine de' Medici later became its most devoted occupant. The Menier family, its owners, opened it to visitors in 1913.
new.tip: Arrive at opening or late in the day to avoid the tour-bus peak. Gardens and the gallery over the river are the highlights.
new.q: Château de Chenonceau, Chenonceaux

new.title: Look over the Loire from the Château royal d'Amboise
new.desc: Charles VIII launched work in 1492 to turn the medieval fortress on a rocky spur into a royal palace. Leonardo da Vinci is buried in the Chapelle Saint-Hubert in the grounds. The gardens give a wide panorama of the Loire valley.
new.tip: A combined ticket with the Clos Lucé is sold. Climb up from the town centre via the Rampe du Château.
new.q: Château royal d'Amboise, Montée de l'Emir Abd el Kader, Amboise

new.title: Step into Leonardo da Vinci's last home at Clos Lucé
new.desc: Francis I gave the manor to Leonardo in 1516 and he lived here until his death on 2 May 1519. The restored rooms include his bedroom, and the park shows full-size models of his machines.
new.tip: Allow two hours for the house and the park of inventions. Combined tickets with the Château royal exist.
new.q: Château du Clos Lucé, Rue du Clos Lucé, Amboise

new.title: Climb the Pagode de Chanteloup in Amboise forest
new.desc: The 44-metre chinoiserie pagoda dates from 1775 and was commissioned by the Duke of Choiseul. It is all that remains of the Château de Chanteloup, destroyed in 1823. The summit overlooks the Loire valley.
new.tip: Open seasonally (the 2026 season ended 11 November), so check dates before planning a visit. Picnic baskets are welcome in the park.
new.q: Pagode de Chanteloup, Route de Bléré, Amboise

new.title: Stroll the Renaissance gardens of Villandry
new.desc: The gardens spread over several terraces and include the famous ornamental kitchen garden and the Love gardens. Dr Joachim Carvallo, a Spaniard, bought the estate in 1906, restored the château and recreated the Renaissance gardens. They are part of the UNESCO-listed Loire Valley.
new.tip: Visit in late spring or summer when the vegetable squares are in full colour. Climb to the belvedere for the best overview.
new.q: Château et jardins de Villandry, Rue Principale, Villandry

new.title: See the Château d'Azay-le-Rideau reflected in the Indre
new.desc: Built between 1518 and 1527 for the financier Gilles Berthelot under Francis I, it is an early French Renaissance masterpiece rising straight out of the water. Balzac called it a diamond in Le Lys dans la vallée.
new.tip: The English-style park around the château is the best place to photograph the reflection. It is run by the Centre des monuments nationaux.
new.q: Château d'Azay-le-Rideau, Rue Balzac, Azay-le-Rideau

new.title: Visit the Sleeping Beauty château at Ussé
new.desc: Set on the edge of Chinon forest above the Indre, the château is tied by tradition to Charles Perrault's Sleeping Beauty and stages scenes from the tale in its rooms. Its gardens are attributed to André Le Nôtre and Chateaubriand's Lebanon cedars stand near the chapel.
new.tip: The château closes for several months each winter, roughly mid-November to mid-February. Check dates before going.
new.q: Château d'Ussé, Rigny-Ussé

new.title: Explore the medieval fortress of Langeais
new.desc: The château was built from 1465 under Louis XI, and Anne of Brittany married Charles VIII here in 1491, tying Brittany to France. Jacques Siegfried bought it in 1886 and restored it with an outstanding collection of tapestries and furniture. It belongs to the Institut de France.
new.tip: It is a five-minute walk from Langeais station. Look for the medieval drawbridge side first.
new.q: Château de Langeais, Place Pierre de Brosse, Langeais

new.title: Walk the ramparts of the Forteresse royale de Chinon
new.desc: The fortress stands on a rocky spur above the Vienne. Henry II of England died here in 1189 and Charles VII met Joan of Arc here in 1429. It reopened to the public in 2003 after major restoration.
new.tip: Terrain is uneven in places. Allow two hours and enjoy the view over the old town from the ramparts.
new.q: Forteresse royale de Chinon, Rue du Château, Chinon

new.title: Visit Rabelais's family farmhouse, La Devinière
new.desc: The 15th-century farmhouse in Seuilly, about 7 km from Chinon, is traditionally identified as the birthplace of François Rabelais. The Indre-et-Loire department bought it in 1948 and the museum opened in 1951. It is the only museum devoted to Rabelais.
new.tip: A sound trail links the museum to the nearby abbey. Combine with a wine tasting in Chinon.
new.q: Musée Rabelais - La Devinière, Seuilly

new.title: Climb the keep and royal lodge of the Cité royale de Loches
new.desc: The great keep is attributed to Foulques Nerra in the early 11th century. In the 1440s Charles VII stayed with Agnès Sorel in the royal lodge. Her tomb lies in the nearby collegiate church of Saint-Ours.
new.tip: Allow at least two hours 15 minutes to visit both sites of the Cité royale. The only entrance is the Porte Royale, on foot.
new.q: Cité royale de Loches, Loches

new.title: Discover Montrésor, one of France's most beautiful villages
new.desc: The medieval fortress dates from the early 11th century under Foulques Nerra and keeps a surviving Renaissance wing. The 19th-century owner Count Xavier Branicki gave the village and château new life and left strong Polish connections. The village belongs to Les Plus Beaux Villages de France.
new.tip: Walk the riverside path along the Indrois for views of the château and village. Check opening days in advance.
new.q: Château de Montrésor, Montrésor

new.title: Gaze over the Vienne and Loire from Candes-Saint-Martin
new.desc: The village stands at the confluence of the Vienne and the Loire. Tradition says Saint Martin died here in 397 in a monastery he founded. The Collégiale Saint-Martin, built in the 12th to 15th centuries, stands on that site and is listed as a historic monument.
new.tip: Walk up to the church viewpoint for the confluence view. The village belongs to Les Plus Beaux Villages de France.
new.q: Collégiale Saint-Martin, Place de l'Église, Candes-Saint-Martin

new.title: Admire the roofline of the Château de Chambord
new.desc: Francis I began this hunting residence in 1519. It has 426 rooms, 365 fireplaces and 77 staircases, and was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage list in 1981. It stands inside the largest walled forest park in Europe.
new.tip: Walk the double-helix staircase and climb to the terraces. Arrive early and rent a bike or boat to see it from outside.
new.q: Château de Chambord, Chambord

new.title: Study four centuries of architecture at the Château royal de Blois
new.desc: The courtyard is framed by four wings that reflect the major styles of French architecture from the Middle Ages to the 17th century. It became the favourite royal residence and political capital under Louis XII in 1498. Napoléon I saved it from demolition in 1810.
new.tip: Open daily with hours varying by season. Look for the Francis I spiral staircase.
new.q: Château royal de Blois, Place du Château, Blois

new.title: Watch the dragon at the Maison de la Magie Robert-Houdin
new.desc: The museum opened in 1998 in a mid-19th-century mansion opposite the château and honours Blois-born illusionist Jean-Eugène Robert-Houdin. It spans five levels, with live magic shows and tours led by illusionists. A dragon emerges from the facade windows every half hour.
new.tip: The 2026 season ran from early April to 1 November, so check dates for 2027. Book show times at the entrance.
new.q: Maison de la Magie Robert-Houdin, 1 Place du Château, Blois

new.title: Recognise Tintin's Moulinsart at the Château de Cheverny
new.desc: Hergé modelled Moulinsart on Cheverny, minus its two outer pavilions. Since 2001 a permanent exhibition, Les Secrets de Moulinsart, has occupied a 700 m2 outbuilding. The de Vibraye family still lives here and has opened it to the public since 1922.
new.tip: Combine with the exhibition and the hound kennels. Budget two hours.
new.q: Château de Cheverny, Cheverny

new.title: Tour the Château de Chaumont-sur-Loire and its art centre
new.desc: A château of the late 15th and early 16th century that blends defensive Gothic with Renaissance comfort. Madame de Staël acquired it in 1810, and the Centre-Val de Loire region bought it in 2007 and runs it as a Centre for Arts and Nature.
new.tip: Grounds open year-round. Reach it by train to Onzain-Chaumont-sur-Loire plus a short taxi ride, or on the Loire à Vélo.
new.q: Domaine de Chaumont-sur-Loire, Chaumont-sur-Loire

new.title: See 327 portraits in the Château de Beauregard gallery
new.desc: The Galerie des Illustres holds 327 portraits of historical figures, created by Paul Ardier from 1617. The château was once a hunting lodge of Francis I and is a listed monument since 1840. The portraits have been restored since 1986.
new.tip: Check the official site for current opening hours before travelling. The park is also worth a walk.
new.q: Château de Beauregard, 12 chemin de la Fontaine, Cellettes

new.title: Cross the drawbridge of the Château de Fougères-sur-Bièvre
new.desc: A fortified medieval castle with a square keep, curtain walls with machicolations and a fortified postern gate. The Lambot family acquired it in 1738, and it is now run by the Centre des monuments nationaux.
new.tip: Visit the garden and the great Council hall. Check seasonal opening dates.
new.q: Château de Fougères-sur-Bièvre, Rue de l'Église, Fougères-sur-Bièvre

new.title: Admire the Gothic facade of Vendôme's Abbaye de la Trinité
new.desc: Geoffroy Martel, count of Vendôme, and his wife Agnès founded the Benedictine abbey around 1033-1034. The Gothic abbey church is known for its western facade, stained glass and choir stalls.
new.tip: Combine with a walk along the Loir channels in the old town.
new.q: Abbaye de la Trinité, Rue de l'Abbaye, Vendôme

new.title: Climb to the ruined castle and park above Vendôme
new.desc: The ruins and terraces of the Bourbon-Vendôme château overlook the town and the Loir valley. Listed as historic monuments, they span the 11th to 17th centuries, and a 19th-century romantic park of about 6 hectares surrounds them.
new.tip: The ruins are reached from the Rampe du Château. Good for a free hilltop view over the town.
new.q: Ruines du château de Vendôme, Rampe du Château, Vendôme

new.title: Explore the castle ruins above Lavardin village
new.desc: The ruined 11th-century castle sits on a rocky promontory above the Loir and has been a classified monument since 1945. It was dismantled in 1589 on the orders of Henri IV. Lavardin is the only village of Loir-et-Cher in Les Plus Beaux Villages de France.
new.tip: A 2026 reopening is announced on one guide, so check hours and access before visiting.
new.q: Château de Lavardin, Lavardin

new.title: Call down the Puits qui parle in the troglodyte village of Trôo
new.desc: The well, about 45 metres deep and dug in the 11th century, amplifies voices at its opening. It is a listed monument and one stop on the Sentier des troglodytes in the Petite Cité de Caractère of Trôo.
new.tip: Speak into the opening for the echo. The village is built vertically with eight staircases, so wear good shoes.
new.q: Puits qui parle, rue du Puits qui parle, Trôo

new.title: See Romanesque frescoes in Montoire's Chapelle Saint-Gilles
new.desc: The former priory chapel, a classified monument, holds painted apses with three Christs in majesty from the 12th and early 13th centuries. It was the priory of the poet Ronsard from 1566 until his death in 1585.
new.tip: The keys are collected from a local association, so check access times. Entry is about 5 euros.
new.q: Chapelle Saint-Gilles, Montoire-sur-le-Loir

new.title: Learn Sologne history at the Musée de Sologne in Romorantin
new.desc: Founded in 1882 by Ovide Scribe, the museum has Musée de France status since 2003 and occupies the Moulin du Chapitre in Romorantin-Lanthenay. It evokes the town's drapery and Matra heritage and the life of the Sologne.
new.tip: Check current temporary exhibitions. Pair with a walk along the Sauldre river through the town.
new.q: Musée de Sologne, Moulin du Chapitre, Romorantin-Lanthenay

new.title: See the moated Château du Moulin in the Sologne
new.desc: Philippe du Moulin, chamberlain to Charles VIII, built this rectangular water castle between 1480 and 1502. It is nicknamed the Pearl of the Sologne and has been listed since 1927. It reopened to the public in spring 2026 after several years closed.
new.tip: Visits at about 8 euros for adults. Confirm opening dates on the official site.
new.q: Château du Moulin, Lassay-sur-Croisne

new.title: Wander the fairy-tale gardens of the Château du Rivau
new.desc: Pierre de Beauvau, chamberlain to Charles VII, received permission in 1442 to fortify the site. The fortress has a keep, a working drawbridge and dry moats, and fourteen themed gardens inspired by tales and legends. The château was classified in 1918.
new.tip: Open roughly April to November, so check dates. It is about 10 km from Chinon.
new.q: Château du Rivau, 9 rue du Château, Lémeré

new.title: Taste puits d'amour at Pâtisserie Bigot in Amboise
new.desc: A family pastry shop and tea room at 2 rue Nationale facing the château, rooted in a bakery opened opposite it in 1913. It is known for puits d'amour, tarte tatin, chocolates and homemade ice cream, plus light meals.
new.tip: Order a puits d'amour with tea in the salon. Reviews mention slow service at peak times.
new.q: Pâtisserie Bigot, 2 Rue Nationale, Amboise

new.title: Taste Chinon wine in the Caves Painctes
new.desc: A network of tuffeau tunnels dug under a hill, said to have inspired Rabelais's Temple of the Dive Bouteille. The guided visit includes a short film, a walk through the Rabelais-themed troglodyte cellars and a tasting.
new.tip: Admission from about 6 euros including the tasting, free under 16. Check seasonal visit times.
new.q: Les Caves Painctes, Impasse des Caves Painctes, Chinon

new.title: Taste single-parcel Cabernet Franc at Domaine Charles Joguet
new.desc: Charles Joguet took over the family property in 1957 and introduced estate bottling and single-vineyard cuvées such as Clos de la Dioterie and Clos du Chêne Vert. The vines are mostly Cabernet Franc, on the left bank of the Vienne.
new.tip: Book a 45-minute discovery tasting of five parcel wines in advance.
new.q: Domaine Charles Joguet, 3 rue de la Vienne, Sazilly

new.title: Eat ring-shaped macarons at Aux Vrais Macarons de Cormery
new.desc: Cormery macarons are small golden rings of ground almonds, sugar and egg whites, traced to the Saint-Paul abbey. The bakery at 8 rue Nationale is run by pastry chef Pascal Debaud, who keeps the old recipe.
new.tip: A second shop, Aux Véritables Macarons de l'Abbaye, is on rue de Montrésor. Check hours before going.
new.q: Aux Vrais Macarons de Cormery, 8 Rue Nationale, Cormery

new.title: Dine on garden vegetables at the Auberge du Bon Laboureur
new.desc: A converted coaching inn from 1786 and a family restaurant of about 100 years, a short walk from the château. Chef Antoine Jeudi cooks seasonal, vegetable-forward menus from its kitchen garden, and it holds a Michelin Plate.
new.tip: Book two to four weeks ahead in high season. Menus are in the upper price range.
new.q: Auberge du Bon Laboureur, 6 rue du Docteur-Bretonneau, Chenonceaux

new.title: Buy Selles-sur-Cher goat cheese at the Fromagerie Moreau
new.desc: Based in a 19th-century farm complex in Pontlevoy, the fromagerie makes AOP Selles-sur-Cher and AOP Sainte-Maure de Touraine goat cheese. The Moreau family ran it from 1879 and Jean-Luc Bilien bought it in 2012. The shop also sells wine, beer, honey and jam.
new.tip: Ask in the shop about tours of the moulding room. Opening hours are not published widely, so call ahead.
new.q: Fromagerie Moreau, Ferme de Bellevue, Pontlevoy

new.title: Buy handmade chocolates at Max Vauché in Blois
new.desc: Pastry chef Max Vauché opened his first boutique on rue du Commerce in Blois in 1986. His main workshop is in Bracieux, where guided visits show cocoa processing.
new.tip: The Bracieux workshop runs tours and chocolate workshops for children and adults. Check current hours.
new.q: Max Vauché chocolatier, 50 rue du Commerce, Blois

new.title: Taste Romorantin white wine at Domaine des Huards
new.desc: Cour-Cheverny is the only appellation for the white Romorantin grape, recognised in 1993. Domaine des Huards, at 30 voie des Huards, offers tasting and sales on site.
new.tip: Try a dry Cour-Cheverny with local goat cheese. Call ahead for tasting hours.
new.q: Domaine des Huards, 30 voie des Huards, Cour-Cheverny

new.title: Taste Bourgueil Cabernet Franc at Domaine des Chesnaies
new.desc: Run by Lamé-Delisle-Boucard since 1869, the estate farms about 44 hectares, mostly Cabernet Franc, in Bourgueil. The family's cellars sit above a network of tuffeau caves, and the estate is certified organic.
new.tip: Confirm visit times directly, as reception hours are not published widely.
new.q: Domaine des Chesnaies, 21 rue de la Galotière, Ingrandes-de-Touraine

new.title: Taste Montlouis Chenin at Maison Laudacius
new.desc: A cooperative cellar founded in 1961 by about 15 winegrowers. A 45-minute visit runs through troglodyte cellars and production areas, followed by a tasting of dry, fruity and sparkling Chenin wines.
new.tip: Book for tastings. The sparkling Jardin des Rois is the house sparkling cuvée.
new.q: Maison Laudacius, 2 route de Saint-Aignan, Montlouis-sur-Loire

new.title: Eat Loire river fish at Au Rendez-Vous des Pêcheurs
new.desc: A fish restaurant at 27 rue du Foix in Blois, started as a fishermen's grocery on the Loire and refreshed by chef Christophe Cosme. Gault&Millau rates it 13/20 for river fish and a wine cellar.
new.tip: Menus from about 29 to 69 euros. Check opening days, as it is closed some days.
new.q: Au Rendez-Vous des Pêcheurs, 27 rue du Foix, Blois

new.title: Dine on Touraine produce at Arbore & Sens in Loches
new.desc: The top table of the medieval city at 22 rue Balzac, led by chef Clément Dumont and rated Table Remarquable by Gault&Millau. Dishes cited include a Loire-inspired caponata and a bone broth with Touraine saffron.
new.tip: Menus run from about 55 to 125 euros. Book ahead.
new.q: Arbore & Sens, 22 rue Balzac, Loches

new.title: Eat a market-driven lunch at Le Malu in Vendôme
new.desc: A well-reviewed Vendôme restaurant rated 13/20 by Gault&Millau with a budget of about 39 to 49 euros. Secondary sources report two consecutive Bib Gourmand awards.
new.tip: Book for weekends. Check the Michelin site for the current Bib Gourmand status.
new.q: Le Malu, Vendôme

new.title: Dine on the terrace of L'Aigle d'Or in Azay-le-Rideau
new.desc: A modern-cuisine restaurant in a country house near the château, with a fireplace and a shaded terrace. Gault&Millau gives it 14/20 under chef Simon Desiles, with menus from about 40 to 85 euros, and Michelin lists it.
new.tip: Closed Monday and Tuesday, with lunch only Thursday to Sunday. Reserve ahead.
new.q: L'Aigle d'Or, 10 avenue Adélaïde-Riche, Azay-le-Rideau

new.title: Lunch facing the château at Le Grand Saint-Michel in Chambord
new.desc: On Place Saint-Louis with a large shaded terrace facing the château. Gault&Millau gives 11/20 and an indicative price of 55 euros, noting views from some tables.
new.tip: Book a table on the terrace in summer. Tables are close together.
new.q: Le Grand Saint-Michel, Place Saint-Louis, Chambord

new.title: Taste Sologne game at the Grand Hôtel du Lion d'Or
new.desc: Chef Didier Clément runs this family house at 69 rue Georges-Clemenceau with his wife Marie-Christine. Michelin lists it with one star, and the cuisine draws on Sologne game in autumn and winter, pond fish and wild herbs.
new.tip: Expect the top price bracket. Contact the restaurant directly to book and check game availability.
new.q: Grand Hôtel du Lion d'Or, 69 rue Georges-Clemenceau, Romorantin-Lanthenay

new.title: Try poires tapées at Maison Hérin in Rivarennes
new.desc: Poire tapée is a traditional Touraine dried pear. Maison Hérin at 14 rue de Quincay offers workshop visits and sells them in the village that also has a dedicated museum.
new.tip: The Maison de la Poire Tapée nearby gives a film and tasting. Check seasonal hours.
new.q: Maison Hérin, 14 rue de Quinçay, Rivarennes

new.title: Taste dry and sweet Vouvray at Domaine Huet
new.desc: Domaine Huet makes only Chenin Blanc from three crus, Le Haut-Lieu, Le Mont and Clos du Bourg, on biodynamic principles. The estate is at 11 rue de la Croix Buisée.
new.tip: Call ahead (+33 2 47 52 78 87) as tasting hours are not published widely. The sparkling brut is good value.
new.q: Domaine Huet, 11 rue de la Croix Buisée, Vouvray
src: https://api-adresse.data.gouv.fr/search/?q=11 rue de la Croix Buisée Vouvray

new.title: See twenty gardens at the Chaumont-sur-Loire garden festival
new.desc: Since 1992, about twenty temporary gardens by international designers are shown each year around a changing theme, from late April to early November. The 2026 theme was Le Jardin fait son cinéma. The estate is on the Loire à Vélo route.
new.tip: The 2026 edition closed on 1 November. Check domaine-chaumont.fr for 2027 dates.
new.q: Domaine de Chaumont-sur-Loire, Rue des Argillons, Chaumont-sur-Loire

new.title: Spend a day at the ZooParc de Beauval
new.desc: The zoo opened in 1980 in Saint-Aignan and is open every day of the year. Tourism listings report more than 35,000 animals, with some species unique in France.
new.tip: Open from 9:00 until dusk. Book tickets online and arrive early.
new.q: ZooParc de Beauval, Avenue du Blanc, Saint-Aignan

new.title: Meet the Tricolour hounds at the Cheverny kennels
new.desc: Cheverny keeps over a hundred Grands Anglo-Français Tricolores, hounds trained for stag hunting. The kennel was created in 1850. The feeding time is a popular show, with dogs waiting for the keeper's permission before eating.
new.tip: Feeding times have changed over the years, so check the château site for the current schedule.
new.q: Chenil du château de Cheverny, Cheverny

new.title: Row or glide on the canal beside the Château de Chambord
new.desc: Electric boats and rowing boats are rented from the quay on the Cosson canal beside the château, with views of the château and its gardens. The rental runs from April to November.
new.tip: Prices in 2014 started around 16 euros for 30 minutes, so check chambord.org for the current price list.
new.q: Embarcadère du château de Chambord, Chambord

new.title: Cycle the greenway from Saint-Dyé-sur-Loire to Chambord
new.desc: The château is about 6 km south of Saint-Dyé-sur-Loire by flat roads, and a greenway links the two towns and continues to Bracieux. A 13 km greenway also runs from Saint-Dyé to Blois on the Loire à Vélo.
new.tip: The 33 km Loop 9, Between Blois and Chambord, starts in Saint-Dyé-sur-Loire and is rated easy.
new.q: Maison de la Loire, 73 rue Nationale, Saint-Dyé-sur-Loire

new.title: Walk or paddle around the Lac de Rillé
new.desc: The lake, also called Lac de Pincemaille, was created in 1977 and hosts over 250 bird species. A leisure base offers rowing boats and canoes as well as fishing. Swimming in the lake itself is not allowed.
new.tip: Swimming is possible at the nearby Lac d'Hommes. Check with the commune about boat rental.
new.q: Lac de Rillé, Rillé

new.title: Walk the Balcons de l'Indrois above Montrésor
new.desc: A riverside path along the Indrois gives an overview of the village, the fortress and the château. Longer loops of 7 to 11 km from Beaumont-Village or Villeloin-Coulangé pass the viewpoint.
new.tip: Free and waymarked. The tourist office (02 47 92 70 71) can give a map.
new.q: Les Balcons de l'Indrois, Montrésor

new.title: Sail on a traditional Loire boat from Blois
new.desc: Observatoire Loire runs guided trips on traditional flat-bottomed boats from the Port de la Creusille in Blois, lasting 1 to 2 hours. Prices start around 13 euros for adults.
new.tip: Reserve ahead and confirm departure times, as trips depend on water levels and season.
new.q: Observatoire Loire, quai Henri Chavigny, Port de la Creusille, Blois

new.title: Watch stone form in the Grottes pétrifiantes de Savonnières
new.desc: The Grottes pétrifiantes de Savonnières are a guided cave visit about 1 km from the Château de Villandry. Water seeping through the rock coats objects with limestone, and the visit lasts roughly an hour.
new.tip: Open daily with a break at lunchtime, according to Tours tourism; check hours and prices by phone before going. Free parking on site.
new.q: Les Grottes pétrifiantes, 61 rue des Grottes Pétrifiantes, Savonnières

new.title: Browse the Sunday market on the quai in Amboise
new.desc: A large market on the Loire bank selling fruit, vegetables, meat, fish and clothing, according to visitor reports. Fridays also have stalls. The weekly market is set up on the banks of the Loire.
new.tip: Sunday morning is the biggest day. The days and hours come from reviews, so check the tourist office.
new.q: Marché d'Amboise, quai du Général de Gaulle, Amboise

new.title: Shop the Wednesday and Saturday market in Loches
new.desc: The market runs twice a week in the town centre below the Cité royale and is described as a showcase of the flavours of the Lochois. It is a good place for local goat cheese and produce.
new.tip: Held Wednesday and Saturday mornings. Visit the Cité royale afterwards.
new.q: Marché de Loches, Centre-ville, Loches

new.title: Join the Rendez-vous de l'histoire festival in Blois
new.desc: Founded in 1998 under mayor Jack Lang, the festival of history holds lectures, debates and a book fair every October at the Château royal, the Halle aux Grains and the CCI campus. The 2026 edition ran 7 to 11 October on the theme of merchants.
new.tip: The festival is held every October. Programmes are published in September.
new.q: Halle aux Grains, Blois

new.title: Tour the Loire châteaux in miniature at Parc Mini-Châteaux
new.desc: Models at 1/25th scale of 44 famous Loire castles stand on a 2-hectare site created in 1996 on the edge of Amboise. In summer, monday evening concerts close the park at sunset.
new.tip: Adults around 16 euros online. Take bus line C from Amboise.
new.q: Parc Mini-Châteaux, Boulevard Saint-Denis Hors, Amboise

new.title: Join the medieval market and parade in Chinon
new.desc: The yearly market takes place on the first Saturday of August in the historic centre with a costumed parade from quai Danton. Entry is free, and the Médiévales run at the Forteresse royale from 2 to 4 August in 2026.
new.tip: Free in the town centre, and the fortress days are paid. Hours differ between listings, so confirm with the town.
new.q: Quai Danton, Chinon

new.title: Hike the Chambord park past its wildlife observation posts
new.desc: A route of about 20 km starts at the Gabillière car park on the D112 and passes roughly ten observation posts in Europe's largest walled forest park. The domain also hosts evening wildlife counts and autumn deer-rut evenings.
new.tip: Registration is required for the evening counts and rut evenings. Dates are listed on chambord.org.
new.q: Parking de la Gabillière, D112, Chambord

new.title: Follow the Sentier des troglodytes through Trôo
new.desc: A walk of about 3.5 km and one hour, starting from the Escalier Saint-Gabriel, one of the village's eight staircases. It passes the collegiate church and the butte with a view of the Loir valley.
new.tip: Free walking circuit. The village is a Petite Cité de Caractère.
new.q: Escalier Saint-Gabriel, Trôo

new.title: Paddle under the arches of Chenonceau on the Cher
new.desc: Canoe trips of about 12 km run from Montrichard past the arches of the Château de Chenonceau. Aventure Canoë sur le Cher has start points at Chisseaux, Saint-Aignan and Chissay, and is announced open from 20 March to 23 December 2026.
new.tip: Family trips are open to children from 6 years. Confirm prices and bookings with the base.
new.q: Aventure Canoë sur le Cher, Chisseaux

new.title: Browse the Saturday market on Place Louis XII in Blois
new.desc: The market stands in the heart of the town beside the royal château. Sources give hours from about 8:30 to 12:45 or 13:15 on Saturday morning.
new.tip: Go early for the best produce. Hours vary by source, so check the Blois tourist office.
new.q: Place Louis XII, Blois

new.title: Walk the Sentier des étangs near La Ferté-Saint-Cyr
new.desc: A circuit through the wooded Sologne, where forests and ponds cover most of the land. It starts from the La Ferté-Saint-Cyr area, in the Romorantin-Lanthenay region.
new.tip: Stay on marked trails in this Natura 2000 area. Wear boots, as paths can be muddy.
new.q: Sentier des étangs, La Ferté-Saint-Cyr

new.title: Paddle the Loire with Loire Kayak at Vineuil
new.desc: Loire Kayak is a canoe base at Vineuil near Blois, open in April, May, June and September and daily in July and August. It offers trips on the Loire in the Loir-et-Cher.
new.tip: Book in advance and confirm hours with the base.
new.q: Loire Kayak, Vineuil
